Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya (JNV) is a system of central‑government schools in India that was established in 1984. The schools are located in every district of the country and are run by the Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (JNVS), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Education (formerly the Ministry of Human Resources Development).  

**Key features of JNVs:**

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Purpose** | To provide quality education to talented children from rural areas, especially those belonging to disadvantaged socio‑economic backgrounds. |
| **Admission** | Students are admitted through a competitive entrance exam (JNV Entrance Examination) held each year. The exam is conducted in the local language. |
| **Curriculum** | The schools follow the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) curriculum and offer classes from Grade 6 to Grade 12. |
| **Boarding** | Most JNVs are residential schools. Students stay in hostels and receive free accommodation, meals, and uniforms. |
| **Facilities** | Modern classrooms, laboratories, libraries, computer labs, sports facilities, and a health centre are standard features. |
| **Funding** | The schools are fully funded by the Government of India; students pay no tuition fees. |
| **Outcome** | JNV graduates often score high in national exams and pursue higher education in engineering, medicine, and other fields. |
